rule: order = the order of the code slides of the deck; the page tab lists the examples by name in this order; each runs as setup + listing, with the library defined in the page

examples.name: Read Alice's transaction field by field
examples.code:
tx = parse_tx(ALICE)                  # to fields
groups = {}
for name, pos, n in tx['spans']:      # every field
    key = name.split(' ')[0]          # first word
    groups[key] = groups.get(key, 0) + n
total = sum(groups.values())          # all bytes

examples.name: A spend updates the UTXO set
examples.code:
prev = PREV_REC['vout'][1]            # the coin
utxo = {(txid(PREV), 1): prev['value']}
before = sorted(utxo.values())
for i in tx['inputs']:                # spent: out
    del utxo[(i['txid'], i['vout'])]
for n, o in enumerate(tx['outputs']): # new: in
    utxo[(txid(ALICE), n)] = o['value']
fee = sum(before) - sum(utxo.values())

examples.name: Four sequence values, three meanings
examples.code:
rows = []
for s in (0xffffffff, 0xfffffffe, 0xfffffffd, 30):
    d = sequence_decode(s)            # BIP68/125
    rows.append((d['hex'], d['rbf_signal'],
                 d['relative_timelock']))

show.expected: [('0xffffffff', False, None), ('0xfffffffe', False, None), ('0xfffffffd', True, None), ('0x0000001e', True, ('blocks', 30))]

examples.name: The 2010 overflow, in five lines
examples.code:
out = 9223372036854277039          # satoshis, each
wrapped = (2 * out) & 0xffffffffffffffff
neg = wrapped >= 2**63               # sign bit set
total = wrapped - 2**64 if neg else wrapped
naive_ok = total <= MAX_MONEY         # old check
fixed_ok = money_range(out)           # each one

examples.name: 569: weight by field
How a txid is made: double SHA-256
examples.code:
leg = serialize(tx, witness=False)    # no witness
h1 = sha256(leg)                      # first hash
h2 = sha256(h1)                       # second hash
shown = h2[::-1].hex()                # reversed
same = shown == txid(ALICE)
